condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Ofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone sharing the same 4-oxo-3-carboxylic acid core, has measured oral bioavailability of 95-100% in healthy volunteers, including absolute bioavailability estimates from oral vs i.v. comparisons.
Levofloxacin, the active enantiomer of ofloxacin, approaches 100% absolute oral bioavailability after 500 mg oral vs intravenous dosing in healthy volunteers.
Trovafloxacin, another fluoroquinolone, has mean absolute oral bioavailability of 87.6% (range 64.8-122.1%) in fasting healthy volunteers.
Antofloxacin is reported as well absorbed with high oral bioavailability in human clinical pharmacokinetic studies.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental oral bioavailability measurement for the exact query molecule is provided; the decision relies on transfer from closely related fluoroquinolones.
The query's physicochemical prior indicates full ionization and low logD, but no query-specific permeability, solubility, or transporter data are available.
The 7-substituent in the query is a fluoroalkene-containing piperidine, which is not identical to the reference fluoroquinolone substituents; its absorption impact is inferred by structural analogy.
No formulation-, dose-, or species-matched data for the exact query are present.
content.decision_summary: Prediction is high. The query is a fluoroquinolone with the same 4-oxo-3-carboxylic acid core and 6-fluoro/8-methoxy/1-cyclopropyl pattern as reference fluoroquinolones whose measured oral bioavailability is 87.6-100% (C04, C13, C14, etc.). The physicochemical prior is uncertain and does not provide affirmative evidence for F < 20%; no contradictory records are present.
